items.title: Inquest date set into death of Jamal Francique, shot by Peel police in Mississauga in 2020
items.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, a 28-year-old man who died after an interaction with Peel police in Mississauga nearly seven years ago, will begin next month. m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Dr. Jennifer M. Dmetrichuk, regional supervising coroner for the Central Region, announced. Francique died on Jan. 9, 2020, following an interaction with Peel Regional Police officers on Jan. 7, 2020. An inquest into his death is mandatory under Ontario’s Coroners Act. The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding his death, and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing future deaths. It is expected to last 11 days and hear from about nine witnesses. Bonnie Goldberg will be the presiding officer, and Roger Shallow will be inquest counsel. The inquest will be held by video conference, and members of the public can watch the proceedings live online.

items.title: Auto thefts down 20 per cent in Mississauga and Brampton, police say
items.summary: Fewer vehicles are being stolen in Peel Region, but police say auto theft remains a top priority. Peel Regional Police say 4,014 vehicles worth about $178 million were stolen in the most recent 12-month period ending in June 2026. That’s down from 5,005 vehicles worth $257 million the year before. That’s a 20 per cent drop in the number of vehicles stolen and a 31 per cent drop in their value, year over year. Police say vehicle thefts have fallen by 50 per cent since 2023. Police also laid 1,217 criminal charges related to auto theft between January 2025 and June 2026. “Auto theft and cargo crime do more than steal property,” police said in a press release. ” While auto theft has declined from its peak, police say it remains a key priority for the service. READ MORE : 229 vehicles stolen in the last 30 days in Mississauga and Brampton Police credit the results to strong partnerships, shared intelligence and coordinated enforcement, along with ongoing investments in auto theft prevention and enforcement and coordinated investigations.

items.title: Mississauga man charged in human trafficking investigation
items.summary: A Mississauga man is facing multiple charges, including human trafficking, after an investigation by London police. The London Police Service (LPS) says it was contacted in June by a woman who reported being the victim of human trafficking, assaults and exploitation dating back to 2019. During the investigation, police learned the suspect had allegedly been involved in similar relationships with multiple women over several years. Investigators received information that one victim had been exploited in the sex trade, that the suspect had financially benefited from her activities, and that he had tried to recruit more women for sexual exploitation. Multiple incidents of violence were also reported, police say. On Oct. 21, members of the LPS Human Trafficking Unit, with help from the Toronto Police Service Emergency Response Team, executed search warrants in Etobicoke and Woodbridge. Police seized a quantity of Canadian cash, four cellphones and multiple Percocet pills. The suspect was arrested in Woodbridge. Jesse Nigel Jones, 32, of Mississauga, has been charged with: He remains in custody and is expected to appear in a London court on Oct. 26.

items.title: Police warn of rise in distraction thefts targeting gold jewellery in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Peel Regional Police are warning residents to be cautious with friendly strangers after an increase in distraction thefts across Mississauga and Brampton. Police say they have investigated more than 230 distraction thefts so far in 2026, and gold jewellery remains one of the most commonly targeted items. According to police, suspects often approach people who are alone and start what seems like a harmless conversation or ask for help. While the victim is distracted, the suspects steal their valuables. “Not every friendly stranger has good intentions,” police said in a social media post. Police say those most at risk include seniors, tourists, people who are alone and people carrying visible valuables. To lower the risk of becoming a victim, police recommend residents: Police are also urging residents to trust their instincts, saying that if something doesn’t feel right, it probably isn’t. A Mississauga senior told INSAUGA Canada she was approached by two people who asked her for directions to a church and then offered her a piece of fake jewellery to get her to come closer. She was wearing a heavy gold necklace at the time. She said she immediately realized it was a distraction theft and ran away.

items.title: John Tory weighs in on the mayoral race — in Mississauga
items.summary: The former Toronto mayor offered praise for Bonnie Crombie and her idea for a subway extension into Mississauga. John Tory speaks at a January 2020 press conference when he was Toronto mayor, alongside then-Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie and Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown. John Tory has expressed support for a mayoral candidate — but not in Toronto. In the final days on the municipal campaign trail, the former mayor weighed in on the highly competitive Mississauga race, where incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish is facing challenges from her predecessor Bonnie Crombie and councillor Alvin Tedjo. ”My experience with Bonnie Crombie was very positive,” said Tory in a Friday night interview. “She has the experience that we probably need, especially now in difficult, challenging times for cities and for the country,” he said, adding that he thinks Crombie’s idea for a subway extension from Kipling Station in Toronto to Square One in downtown Mississauga is a good one, adding a needed seamless regional connection. ” The affection appears mutual, with Crombie saying in a statement to the Star that Tory’s “confidence in my experience and economic leadership means a great deal” and that if elected she will be tapping Tory to help lead her push for the subway extension.

items.title: Pop-up shop selling high-end clothes for less opens in Square One in Mississauga
items.summary: A well-known store selling pre-owned high-end designer clothes, bags, and jewellery at lower prices has opened its first Ontario pop-up store in Mississauga. , Saint Laurent, and Louis Vuitton), recently opened its third pop-up at Square One Shopping Centre. Although the consignment brand operates a permanent brick-and-mortar location in Toronto’s Yorkville neighbourhood, its latest Holt Renfrew-partnered pop-up, is the first in the province. When asked why the brand picked Square One as the site of its latest temporary store, Mine & Yours chief operating officer Danielle Loftus told INSAUGA Canada that the bustling GTA shopping centre is a good fit for a company specializing in more attainable high-end goods. “There’s a very strong emerging market for the luxury sector within the GTA. We know we have a lot of customers commuting in to see us in the city,” she says, adding that the 13-year-old Vancouver-based company has also attracted buyers from across the country to its e-commerce platform. ” While the brand isn’t new, its pop-up partnership with Holt Renfrew is relatively recent. Last year, Mine & Yours opened a pop-up in Calgary, and this past spring, a second one. The brand also has plans to open a pop-up in Montreal.

items.title: No GO Trains Between Union and Aldershot This Weekend as Lakeshore West Work Continues
items.summary: Insauga.com reports GO Transit is warning riders to plan ahead this weekend, Oct. 24 and 25, as a major construction closure cancels train service on a large stretch of the Lakeshore West line. According to the outlet, there will be no trains running between Aldershot GO and Union Station, though GO will keep operating trains between Niagara Falls and Aldershot and run replacement buses between West Harbour GO and Union Station Bus Terminal. The outlet reports the closure leaves Appleby, Bronte, Port Credit, Long Branch, Mimico and Exhibition GO stations without GO service for the weekend, forcing passengers to connect through local transit systems such as Burlington Transit, Oakville Transit, MiWay and the TTC. According to GO, riders leaving from Appleby can take Oakville Transit's Route 14A to Oakville GO and catch a bus to Union Station, a trip expected to take about one hour and 52 minutes. The outlet reports a similar route from Bronte GO via Oakville Transit Route 18 takes roughly one hour and 21 minutes, while Port Credit GO riders can connect through MiWay Route 2 and GO bus Route 21 for a trip of about one hour and 32 minutes.

items.title: Trade-Show Floor Full of Unproven Products Greets Visitors at Mississauga's 'Science-Backed' Menopause Event
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports a 'backed by science' menopause show at Mississauga's International Centre drew attendees looking for reliable health information, only to confront a trade-show floor packed with more than 90 booths selling products that didn't always meet that standard. According to the outlet, attendee Catharine Adams said she expected help sorting through misinformation but instead had to walk past vendors hawking a '100 per cent accurate' menopause test, a bath-salt 'menopause bundle,' a four-week 'perimenopause reset' and various detox, nutrition and anti-aging products before reaching the event's expert sessions. The outlet reports the show also featured a booth promoting an oxygen delivery system marketed under the name 'V Zone,' part of a broader array of exhibitors promising solutions for insomnia, joint pain, brain fog and cardiovascular health risks tied to menopause. The Star reports the show highlighted a women's health issue that has long been stigmatized and underserved by the public health-care system, a gap that private clinics and wellness brands have rushed to fill, not always with evidence-based offerings. According to the outlet, Jennifer Thompson, who founded the Herstasis Foundation to fight menopause misinformation with free evidence-based resources, said the situation 'really makes me mad' and described her non-profit's booth as a 'purple cow' standing out among the show's many commercial interests.

items.title: ‘I’m trying to propose to you’: Mississauga couple gets engaged mid-race at Toronto Waterfront Marathon
items.summary: A couple from Mississauga took the phrase “running off together” to heart, getting engaged mid-race at the TCS Toronto Waterfront Marathon last Sunday and going viral in the process. Gowsic Thevendran, 37, popped the question to his girlfriend of two years, Shaarujaa Nadarajah, 31, before parting ways at Bay and Wellington streets as Thevendran was running the full marathon and Nadarajah the half. The proposal was captured on camera, with the video going viral on social media, accumulating more than 450,000 views on Instagram alone. “I was just in the moment, and I was really happy,” Shaarujaa Nadarajah said in an interview with CTV News Toronto on Friday. “There was a big crowd around us ... ” Nadarajah and Thevendran connected over Bumble in September 2024, a dating app where the woman makes the first move to strike up a conversation with a potential suitor. It had been about a week since Thevendran moved to Mississauga from Montreal for a new job. Nadarajah said she had a “funny rule” for dating at that time. “I just had a rule that I don’t date like suburban men,” Nadarajah said. But Thevendran was one worth breaking the rules for.

items.title: Luxury resale comes to Mississauga’s Square One: Designer shop Mine & Yours opens at Holt Renfrew
items.summary: The pop-up features a “curated selection of pre-loved” designer handbags, apparel and accessories. Mine and Yours opened a location at Holt Renfrew Square One on Oct. 6. Designer fashion resale company Mine & Yours is expanding its partnership with retailer Holt Renfrew with the opening of a pop-up location in Mississauga. The new location, at Holt Renfrew in Square One mall, opened Oct. 6 and marks Mine & Yours’ third pop-up with Holt Renfrew and its first in Ontario. Mine & Yours also operates two pop-up activations with Holt Renfrew in Calgary. ” The company added that the partnership reflects the continued evolution of luxury retail as resale becomes an increasingly important part of how customers shop. “Through its growing partnership with Holt Renfrew, Mine & Yours is extending the life cycle of exceptional fashion while making circular luxury more accessible to customers across Canada,” the company said.

This makes Mississauga 173rd out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. As of July 1, 2026 in Ontario, some previously mandatory accident benefits are now optional. ca data, drivers in Mississauga pay about $3,078 per year for auto insurance as of March 2026. Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. 2% higher. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5K area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year.
